**Finding submitted: MISSING (medium severity) — no post-termination transition or data-return obligation.**

What I found:
- **§ 14 (Termination)** only addresses how long TrueLink keeps serving after our notice — nothing about giving our data back.
- **§ 13 (Term)** actually runs *against* us: it makes Client responsible for arranging a new name server within 30 days and a new hosting environment within 60 days, with no reciprocal vendor migration duty.
- **§ 10 (Confidentiality)** has no return-of-materials mechanic, and a document-wide search for "return" / "Client Data" found nothing relevant — only a mailing reference.
- Material exposure: TrueLink hosts our Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property and borrower and loan data (expressly deemed Client Proprietary Information under § 10(c)), so an exit with no return right is a real walk-away risk.

Redline inserted after § 14 (validated `ok:true`), tracking the preferred position: (a) up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates on request; (b) return of our data in a commonly used, machine-readable format within 30 days; (c) deletion thereafter with written certification.

Drafting note: I anchored the clause inside § 14 deliberately — § 24 provides that Sections 1 and 5 through 30 survive expiration or termination, so the new obligation survives without needing a separate survival amendment. I also mirrored the document's own defined terms (Client Content, Client's Intellectual Property, Client Proprietary Information) rather than importing "Customer Data," which is undefined here. The comment offers the 90-day fallback.
